messages:
Zoe: Quick kickoff — we need a tight benchmark narrative for the product launch. Scope: three hero visuals (latency profile, cost curve, batching impact), short webinar, and a simple inbound lead form. Target: deck draft by Monday EOD.

Arun: I can own visuals. Plan: composite chart with 95p latency (ms) on left axis and $/1k tokens on right, plus two supporting panels: batching benefit and sequence-length heatmap. Will annotate SLO bands and add tooltip blurbs for slides.

Priya: Running targeted traces across tiny/medium/large model configs and hosted/dedicated/private pools. Will capture cold vs warm KV cache and a few batch-size slices. ETA: tonight; pushing CSVs and traces to bench.

Nina: Messaging idea: Hero headline option A: "Latency you can count on" (platform buyers). Option B: "Shrink inference spend, keep the same outputs" (builders). We'll A/B headlines in the landing and try different CTA copy.

Dan: I'll build a compact cost table showing $/1k tokens at 1k/10k/100k with batching multipliers and add an explicit note about where batching yields the best returns. Also propose a tiny trade-off matrix (latency vs cost vs throughput).

Omar: Inbound form prototype: fields = company_size, priority (latency | cost), monthly_token_range, contact_role. Routing rules: priority=latency -> Solutions (Enterprise owners); priority=cost -> Growth SDRs. Include hidden campaign_id + utm for attribution. I can mock the Zapier flow and SFDC owner mapping.

Zoe: Good. Make sure CTAs map to different forms: "Get a latency snapshot" vs "Estimate my inference spend". We want clear lead scoring tags added on submit.

bench-bot: New run posted: https://bench.redwood/run/1739900012  includes 95p metrics, CSV export, and trace bundles labelled by model/batch/kv_state.

Arun: Visual notes: show lines per deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), use faint bars for cost so lines stay readable. Add an inset GIF showing cache cold -> warm latency drop for the narrative.

Priya: Raw traces: https://bench.redwood/traces/1739900012/raw  short/long sequences included. Early results: dedicated pools show pronounced $/1k reductions at higher batch sizes for short sequences. I'll annotate ranges where autoscaling changes the slope.

Nina: Webinar sketch: 25m deck (why predictable latency matters, demo of metrics + charts), 20m case study walk-through, 15m product Q&A. Promo title option: "Production Inference: predictable latency, measurable economics." Keep it punchy for socials.

Dan: One more visual: small matrix showing fallback routing (hosted -> dedicated -> private) and expected cost/latency deltas per step. Helpful for sales to explain trade-offs.

Omar: Prototype link (mock): https://internal.redwood/marketing/proto-form-17399 and routing doc: https://internal.redwood/marketing/routing-17399. I'll include SFDC field mappings and sample Zapier steps.

Zoe: Action items summary: Arun -> 3 hero visuals + GIF + short curl snippet for blog; Priya -> finalize traces + CSVs + percent deltas; Omar -> form prototype + routing map; Nina -> two landing copy variants + webinar outline; Dan -> cost delta table + fallback slide. I'll assemble the deck and schedule a review on Tue 10am.

Arun: Curl snippet for the blog I'll include (short example):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-medium","input":"Hi"}' | jq '{latency_ms: .latency_ms, tokens: .tokens}'
```
Then show how to compute $/1k tokens from token_count and billing headers.

Priya: bench-bot note: cold->warm cache GIF will come from traces labeled kv_cold -> kv_warm. I'll export a 3-frame GIF and a short caption explaining why warm cache reduces tail latency.

Nina: Landing variants uploaded to Drive: https://drive.redwood/marketing/bench-landing-17399. I'll keep public-facing copy simple and put the technical appendix behind a "see technical notes" link.

Dan: For social cards, I'll prepare one short chart snippet and a one-line punch: "Get predictable latency at scale — and lower inference spend." We'll test variants with cost-first and latency-first hooks.

Omar: Routing detail: if priority=latency & company_size=Enterprise -> SFDC owner Solutions_EU; if priority=cost & company_size=SMB -> Growth_SDR_US. Add campaign_id param to URL so closes credit is tracked.

bench-bot: Reminder: use benchmark-deck-v2 template: https://internal.redwood/templates/benchmark-deck-v2

Zoe: Excellent. Keep language customer-facing on landing, preserve the infra details for the appendix. Deck draft due Mon EOD; comment deadline Tue 9:30 if you can't make the sync. Thanks everyone :rocket:
